options.text: It evaluates to false without throwing any exception.
It causes a compile-time syntax error because instanceof requires non-null operands.

explanation: In Java, the instanceof operator is null-safe; if the left-hand operand evaluates to null, the expression always returns false without throwing NullPointerException.

A runtime NoSuchMethodError is thrown by the JVM bytecode interpreter.
A NullPointerException is thrown because the target object reference is null.
The static method executes normally because static dispatch does not dereference the instance.

explanation: Static method calls are resolved at compile time using the declared reference type. The JVM does not dereference the instance variable at runtime, so no NullPointerException is thrown.
